name: Nebuchadnezzar
description: Emperor living at the time of Divided Monarchy

points: In Jehoiakim's days Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up, and Jehoiakim became his servant three years, then turned and rebelled against him.

note.label: 2 Kings 24: Judah Carried Away for the Sins of Manasseh

points: The servants of Nebuchadnezzar came up against Jerusalem and besieged it, and the king himself came against the city while it was besieged.

note.label: 2 Kings 24: Judah Carried Away for the Sins of Manasseh

points: In the ninth year of Zedekiah's reign Nebuchadnezzar came with all his host against Jerusalem, pitched against it, and built forts round about it.

note.label: 2 Kings 25: The Fall of Jerusalem and the Burning of the Temple

points: In the fifth month of the nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard came to Jerusalem.

note.label: 2 Kings 25: The Fall of Jerusalem and the Burning of the Temple

points: Over the people left in the land Nebuchadnezzar made Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, governor.

note.label: 2 Kings 25: The Fall of Jerusalem and the Burning of the Temple

points: The priestly line from Aaron is traced through Eleazar, Phinehas, and on down to Jehozadak, who went into captivity when the Most High carried away Judah and Jerusalem by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 6: The Sons of Levi and the Priesthood

points: Nebuchadnezzar also carries off the vessels of the house of the Lord to Babylon and puts them in his temple. The Most High set a wicked king over the land because his own people would not do what he said.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 36: The Captivity of Judah into Babylon

points: When the year is expired, Nebuchadnezzar sends and brings him to Babylon with the goodly vessels of the house of the Lord, and makes Zedekiah his brother king over Judah.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 36: The Captivity of Judah into Babylon

points: He rebels against Nebuchadnezzar who had made him swear by God, and stiffens his neck and hardens his heart from turning to the Lord God of Israel. The chief priests and people transgress very much after all the abominations of the heathen and pollute the house of the Lord.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 36: The Captivity of Judah into Babylon

points: Cyrus brings out the vessels of the house of the Lord that Nebuchadnezzar had carried from Jerusalem and stored among his own goods.

note.label: Ezra 1: Cyrus Stirred Up to Send Israel Home

points: These are the children of the province who came up out of captivity, whom Nebuchadnezzar had carried away, returning each man to his own city in Jerusalem and Judah.

note.label: Ezra 2: The Register of Those Who Returned

points: They confessed that the fathers provoked the God of heaven, who delivered them into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar and carried them to Babylon. This captivity is read in Second Kings, where Assyria took Israel and later Babylon took Judah.

note.label: Ezra 5: The Prophets Rise Up To Build

points: Cyrus is called king of Babylon because he conquered Babylon and took possession of all it held, though he reigned out of Persia. He restored the gold and silver vessels Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the temple.

note.label: Ezra 5: The Prophets Rise Up To Build

points: There was a certain Jew in Shushan named Mordecai, son of Jair, a Benjamite carried away from Jerusalem with the captivity taken with Jeconiah king of Judah whom Nebuchadnezzar carried away. This gives the lapse of time telling when Mordecai was put into captivity.

note.label: Esther 2: Esther Made Queen and Mordecai Uncovers the Plot

points: King Zedekiah sends Pashur and Zephaniah the priest to ask Jeremiah to inquire of the Most High, hoping He will deal with them according to His wondrous works while Nebuchadnezzar makes war on them.

note.label: Jeremiah 21: The Way of Life and the Way of Death

points: Afterward He will deliver Zedekiah, his servants, and the people into Nebuchadnezzar's hand, to be smitten with the sword without pity or mercy.

note.label: Jeremiah 21: The Way of Life and the Way of Death

points: The Most High shows Jeremiah two baskets of figs set before the temple after Nebuchadnezzar had carried Jeconiah, the princes of Judah, the carpenters, and the smiths away captive to Babylon.

note.label: Jeremiah 24: The Two Baskets of Figs

points: The word came to Jeremiah in the fourth year of Jehoiakim, the first year of Nebuchadnezzar, recounting that for twenty-three years, from the thirteenth year of Josiah, the Most High had risen early and spoken but the people would not hearken.

note.label: Jeremiah 25: The Seventy Years Captivity and the Cup of Fury

points: The Lord calls Nebuchadnezzar my servant and sends him against Judah and all the nations round about to utterly destroy them. Nebuchadnezzar is the analogy for Trump: the Lord uses America today to bring judgment on Lebanon, Saudi Arabia and every neighbour of Jerusalem, and the chapter is twofold, ancient Babylon and the last days.

note.label: Trump Is Fulfilling God's Prophecy

points: Because they would not hear, the Most High will send and take all the families of the north and Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon, His servant, against this land to utterly destroy it and make it a perpetual desolation, an astonishment, and a hissing.

note.label: Jeremiah 25: The Seventy Years Captivity and the Cup of Fury

points: The nation and kingdom that will not serve Nebuchadnezzar and will not put its neck under the yoke of Babylon the Most High will punish with the sword, the famine, and the pestilence until they are consumed.

note.label: Jeremiah 27: The Yoke of Babylon

points: He said thus saith the Lord, even so will I break the yoke of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon from the neck of all nations within two full years; and Jeremiah went his way.

note.label: Jeremiah 28: Hananiah the False Prophet

points: The Most High had put a yoke of iron upon the neck of all these nations that they may serve Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, who was the superpower at this time, and He gave him the beasts of the field also.

note.label: Jeremiah 28: Hananiah the False Prophet

points: Jeremiah sent a letter from Jerusalem to the residue of the elders, the priests, the prophets, and all the people whom Nebuchadnezzar had carried captive to Babylon, after Jeconiah, the queen, the eunuchs, the princes, the carpenters, and the smiths had departed.

note.label: Jeremiah 29: The Letter to the Captives

points: Concerning Ahab the son of Kolaiah and Zedekiah the son of Maaseiah, who prophesied a lie in His name, the Most High would deliver them into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar to be slain before the captives' eyes.

note.label: Jeremiah 29: The Letter to the Captives

points: The Most High answers that He is the God of all flesh and nothing is too hard for Him; He will give the city into the hand of the Chaldeans and Nebuchadnezzar, who will set fire on it and burn it.

note.label: Jeremiah 32: Buying the Field of Redemption

points: The word came when Nebuchadnezzar and all his army fought against Jerusalem: Jeremiah is to tell Zedekiah that the Most High will give the city into Babylon's hand to be burned with fire, and Zedekiah shall not escape.

note.label: Jeremiah 34: Liberty Proclaimed and Then Revoked

points: King Zedekiah the son of Josiah reigns in place of Coniah, whom Nebuchadnezzar made king in the land of Judah, but neither he nor his servants nor the people hearken to the words of the Most High spoken by Jeremiah.

note.label: Jeremiah 37: The Prophet Arrested and Imprisoned

points: The Chaldean army pursues and overtakes Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho, and they bring him up to Nebuchadnezzar at Riblah, where the king of Babylon slays Zedekiah's sons and all the nobles of Judah before his eyes, then puts out Zedekiah's eyes, binds him with chains for Babylon, and burns the king's house and the houses of the people, breaking down the walls of Jerusalem.

note.label: Jeremiah 39: The Fall of Jerusalem

points: Nebuchadnezzar gives charge concerning Jeremiah that he be taken, looked to well, and done no harm, but treated as he himself shall say.

note.label: Jeremiah 39: The Fall of Jerusalem

points: The Most High declared He would send for Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon, His servant, set his throne upon those hidden stones, spread his royal pavilion over them, and smite the land of Egypt.

note.label: Jeremiah 43: The Proud Men Reject the Word and Flee to Egypt

points: The word of the Most High came to Jeremiah against the gentiles, against Egypt and the army of Pharaoh-necho king of Egypt by the river Euphrates at Carchemish, which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon smote in the fourth year of Jehoiakim.

note.label: Jeremiah 46: The Prophecy Against Egypt

points: Concerning Kedar and the kingdoms of Hazor, which Nebuchadnezzar shall smite: arise and spoil the men of the east; their tents, flocks, and camels are taken, and fear is on every side.

note.label: Jeremiah 49: Judgment on Ammon, Edom, Damascus, Kedar, and Elam

points: Israel is a scattered sheep: first Assyria devoured the northern kingdom and last Nebuchadnezzar broke Judah's bones. When both kingdoms fell Edom had no more threat, and that was when he found the time to grow and rise.

note.label: Edom: The Robbers of thy people revealed past and present

points: Israel is a scattered sheep the lions have driven away; first the king of Assyria devoured him, and last Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon broke his bones. The Most High will punish the king of Babylon as he punished Assyria.

note.label: Jeremiah 50: The Fall of Babylon and the Return of Israel

points: Nebuchadnezzar has devoured Israel, crushed her, made her an empty vessel, and swallowed her like a dragon. Let the violence done to Zion be upon Babylon, and her blood upon the inhabitants of Chaldea.

note.label: Jeremiah 51: The Full Recompense of Babylon

points: In the ninth year of his reign Nebuchadnezzar and all his army came against Jerusalem, pitched against it, and built forts round about, and the city was besieged until the eleventh year of Zedekiah.

note.label: Jeremiah 52: The Fall of Jerusalem and the Puppet King Zedekiah

points: These are the numbers Nebuchadnezzar carried away captive: in the seventh year 3,023 Jews, in the eighteenth year 832 persons from Jerusalem, and in the twenty-third year Nebuzaradan carried away 745 persons, four thousand and six hundred in all.

note.label: Jeremiah 52: The Fall of Jerusalem and the Puppet King Zedekiah

points: The Most High will bring Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, a king of kings from the north, with horses, chariots, and horsemen, to slay her daughters, build a fort, cast a mount, and set engines of war against her walls and towers. Babylon serves as His sword against the nations that thought our downfall was their gain.

note.label: Ezekiel 26: The Fall of Tyrus

points: In the twenty-seventh year the word came that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon caused his army to serve a great service against Tyrus, yet had no wages for it, every head made bald and every shoulder peeled.

note.label: Ezekiel 29: The Judgment Against Pharaoh and Egypt

points: In the third year of Jehoiakim king of Judah, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to Jerusalem and besieged it, and the Most High gave Jehoiakim into his hand with part of the vessels of the house of God.

note.label: Daniel 1: The Best of Israel Carried to Babylon

points: Then the king Nebuchadnezzar fell upon his face, and worshipped Daniel, and commanded that they should offer an oblation and sweet odours unto him. The king answered unto Daniel, and said, Of a truth it is, that your God is a God of gods, and a Lord of kings, and a revealer of secrets. Of what? Of secrets.

note.label: When God Reveals His Secrets!

points: Nebuchadnezzar the king made an image of gold, whose height was threescore cubits, and the breadth thereof six cubits: he set it up in the plain of Dura, in the province of Babylon. So Nebuchadnezzar set up the large statue.

note.label: Unity: The Sweet Savor Of Salvation

points: Nebuchadnezzar the king made an image of gold and gathered the princes, the governors, the captains, the judges, the treasurers, the counsellors, the sheriffs, and all the rulers of the provinces to the dedication of the image. Nebuchadnezzar had set up a one world religion. It is the same thing they are trying to do today.

note.label: Agree Together | Bound Not Bondage

points: Nebuchadnezzar made an image of gold, threescore cubits high and six cubits broad, and set it up in the plain of Dura, then gathered the princes, governors, captains, judges, treasurers, counsellors, sheriffs, and rulers to its dedication.

note.label: Daniel 3: The Fiery Furnace and the Servants of the Most High

points: That at what time ye hear the sound of the cornet, flute, harp, sackbut, psaltery, dulcimer, and all kinds of musick, ye fall down and worship the golden image that Nebuchadnezzar the king hath set up. So he said, hey, when you hear this, everybody has got to bow down and worship. Let us see, did Daniel follow the example that Mattathias left, that they did not hearken to the king's words to go from their religion?

note.label: Unity: The Sweet Savor Of Salvation

points: Then Nebuchadnezzar in his rage and fury commanded to bring Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. Then they brought these men before the king. Nebuchadnezzar spake and said unto them, Is it true, O Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, do not ye serve my gods, nor worship the golden image which I have set up? So he came and questioned them. We know the story. We are running out of time. But the point is they faced death right in front of them and they did not waver. They did not waver.

note.label: Unity: The Sweet Savor Of Salvation

points: Full of fury, Nebuchadnezzar commanded the furnace heated seven times more than usual and had his mighty men bind the three in their coats and garments and cast them in.

note.label: Daniel 3: The Fiery Furnace and the Servants of the Most High

points: Nebuchadnezzar blessed the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, who sent his angel to deliver the servants that trusted in him and would not serve nor worship any god except their own God.

note.label: Daniel 3: The Fiery Furnace and the Servants of the Most High

points: At the end of the days, Nebuchadnezzar lifted up his eyes unto heaven, and his understanding returned, and he blessed the Most High: all the inhabitants of the earth are reputed as nothing; none can stay his hand, or say unto him, What doest thou? And those that walk in pride he is able to abase. Do not let your pride pull you aside from God; humble yourself before he draws the picture for you.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart Hath Deceived Thee!

points: At the end of the days Nebuchadnezzar lifted his eyes to heaven, his understanding returned, and he blessed and honoured the Most High, whose dominion is everlasting and before whom all the inhabitants of the earth are reputed as nothing.

note.label: Daniel 4: Nebuchadnezzar Abased Until He Knew the Most High Rules

points: Belshazzar the king made a great feast to a thousand of his lords and, while tasting the wine, commanded the golden and silver vessels his father Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the temple in Jerusalem be brought so he, his princes, wives, and concubines might drink in them.

note.label: Daniel 5: The Handwriting on the Wall

points: The queen came into the banquet house and told the king of the man Daniel, in whom is the spirit of the holy gods, whom Nebuchadnezzar his father had made master of the magicians because an excellent spirit, knowledge, and understanding were found in him.

note.label: Daniel 5: The Handwriting on the Wall
